questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: South Australia was founded in 1836. Unlike New South Wales, its settlers were meant to be free people who paid for their own land. Which description fits South Australia best?
choices: A colony built to hold convicts
A colony planned for free settlers
A fort built to guard the coast
A mission run only by the army
questions.explanation: South Australia was planned as a colony for free settlers, not convicts.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: In the 1830s, many free settlers moved to the Port Phillip district, where Melbourne now stands. What was a main economic reason?
choices: To dig for gold on the first day
To find grassy land for sheep and wool
To build a railway to Perth
questions.explanation: Wool sold well, and the district had plenty of grass for sheep to graze.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Moreton Bay (near Brisbane) was set up as a convict settlement in 1824. Who was it mainly meant for?
choices: Convicts who had reoffended in New South Wales
questions.explanation: Moreton Bay was a place of harsher punishment for convicts who had committed more crimes in the colony.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: As colonists fenced off land for farms, what was a common effect on First Nations peoples?
choices: They gained more land to hunt on
They lost access to waterholes, food sources and special places
They were given the farms to run
Their languages became the colony's main languages
questions.explanation: Taking over land cut First Nations peoples off from the water, food and places that were important to them.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A convict in a colony was given a ticket of leave. What did it allow him to do?
choices: Sail home to Britain straight away
Work for himself in a set district
Stop all work for the rest of his life
questions.explanation: A ticket of leave let a well-behaved convict work for himself in an area, before his sentence was finished.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Pemulwuy was a Bidjigal man from the Sydney area. What part did he play in colonial history?
choices: He led resistance against colonists taking over land
He drew the first map of Australia
questions.explanation: Pemulwuy led his people in defending their land against the colonists around Sydney.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: In 1862, John McDouall Stuart's expedition crossed the continent and returned safely. Which journey did it make?
choices: Crossing Australia from south to north
questions.explanation: Stuart's team crossed the continent from the south coast to the north coast.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: In the 1840s, Caroline Chisholm became well known in colonial New South Wales. What did she mainly do?
choices: Helped new immigrant women and families find homes and work
Found a way to cross the Blue Mountains
questions.explanation: Caroline Chisholm helped newly arrived women and families find safe places to live and jobs.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Parramatta, Wollongong and Wagga Wagga all have names that come from which source?
questions.explanation: These names come from First Nations languages, which shows who first lived in these places.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Many families in a suburb came from Vietnam. Each year they hold a Lunar New Year street festival. How does this shape the suburb?
choices: It makes the suburb known for its food, culture and celebrations
questions.explanation: People's traditions, food and festivals add to what makes a place special.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: In northern Australia, which months are usually called the tropical cyclone season?
questions.explanation: Cyclones mostly happen in the warm, wet months from November to April.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: The fire danger rating for tomorrow is Catastrophic. What is the safest plan for a family in a bushfire area?
choices: Stay and water the garden all day
Leave early for a safer place
Wait to see if smoke appears first
questions.explanation: On the worst fire days, fires can be too fierce to fight, so leaving early is the safest choice.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: In federal elections, who must vote in Australia?
choices: Only people who own a house
Anyone aged 16 or older who lives here
Only members of a political party
questions.explanation: Voting is compulsory for enrolled Australian citizens aged 18 and over.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Your local member of the House of Representatives has been elected. What is their main job?
choices: To teach at the local school
To represent the people of their area in parliament
To pick the winners of sport finals
To run the local police station
questions.explanation: An elected member speaks for the people in their area when laws are discussed.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Voters mark their ballot paper in a private booth and fold it. Why is a secret ballot an important feature of democracy?
choices: People can choose freely without anyone knowing or pressuring them
It lets the winner be picked early
questions.explanation: Keeping votes secret means no one can pressure you, so you can choose freely.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Neighbours want a safe crossing near their school. Which action best shows citizens working together towards that goal?
choices: Each person complains quietly at home
They write a joint petition and send it to the council
They paint their own crossing without asking
They wait for someone else to fix it
questions.explanation: A petition shows many people sharing a goal and asking the council to act.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A Landcare group, where volunteers plant trees together, is an example of citizens with shared values working towards a goal.
questions.explanation: The volunteers share the value of caring for the environment and work together to do it.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A farmer owns a tractor to help grow wheat. Which type of resource is the tractor?
questions.explanation: Tractors are made by people and used to produce other goods, so they are capital resources.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Which of these is a natural resource used to make electricity in some Australian power stations?
questions.explanation: Coal comes from the ground and is burned to make electricity. The others are made by people or are people.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A bakery uses flour, ovens and bakers to make bread. Which one is the human resource?
questions.explanation: Human resources are the work, skills and ideas of people, so the bakers count.
